newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hitachi sees S$90-$100 mln from upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi sees S$90-$100 mln from upgrade.

text.p: Ship repair company Hitachi Zosen Singapore Ltd expects an annual revenue of Singapore $90-$100 million in shipbuilding after its Singapore yard is upgraded, executive chairman Takeshi Tenjin said on Tuesday.

The subsidiary of Osaka-based shipbuilder Hitachi Zosen Corp is scheduled to complete its S$15 million berth extension next week after a 100-tonne lifting crane is installed, Tenjin told Reuters in an interview.
"I can visualise S$90 million to S$100 million per year in additional revenue from the expansion," Tenjin said.
"We are trying to build about four ships of about 20,000 deadweight tonnes (dwt) each per year," he added.
The extension of the slipway to 230 metres from 127 metres would allow the yard to build bulk carriers of up to 30,000 dwt.
Tenjin said the target includes the S$100 million contract it won in November to build four ships to be sold to buyers nominated by Clipper Shipping Ltd.
The first vessel would be delivered at the end of May next year with the last in May 1999, he said.
Hitachi is now engaged mainly in ship repair but has a building capacity for product carriers of 7,900-9,900 tonnes.
For financial year ended March 31, 1996, the group's net profit doubled to S$6.30 million from S$3.04 million.
Turnover rose to S$224.93 million from S$188.51 million, including a record S$82.5 million turnover from shipbuilding.
Ship repair turnover, however, slipped 9.1 percent to S$131.7 million. It is expected to announce its results for year ended March 31, 1997 later June.
